newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-STEVE WAUGH, ELLIOTT IN FORM AS AUSTRALIA DRAW.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STEVE WAUGH, ELLIOTT IN FORM AS AUSTRALIA DRAW.

text.p: Australia gained valuable batting practice ahead of next week's second test against England, with Matthew Elliott and Steve Waugh striking centuries in the tourists' drawn match against Nottinghamshire on Friday.
Resuming at 51 for one in reply to Notts' first innings score of 239, Australia batted through the day with opener Elliott hitting 127 and Waugh 115.
Middle-order batsman Michael Bevan was also in fine touch and remained unbeaten on 75 when rain ended the match early with Australia on 398 for five.
Elliott reached his century with a six over square leg and his 212-ball innings also included 14 fours. Waugh's 115 came in just 137 balls with 11 boundaries.
"I didn't have the best of starts to the tour and I was also feeling a knee (injury) in the early weeks," Elliott said.
"But I'm in much better nick now and today I was very comfortable at the crease. I personally can't wait for the Lord's test. I think it's going to be one hell of a game."
Of Australia's test players only Mark Waugh failed to make a big score, falling for 29.
Opener Michael Slater went on Thursday for 14 and on Friday Ricky Ponting (19) was given out lbw to the fifth ball of the day.

Mark Waugh, who twice fell cheaply in Australia's nine-wicket defeat in the first test, is likely to be given another chance against county champions Leicestershire in a three-day match starting on Saturday.
